title: Efficient On-Device Machine Learning with a Biologically-Plausible Forward-Only Algorithm
problem: Backpropagation-based DNN training on IoT and wearable edge devices is infeasible due to excessive memory (activations must be stored), energy consumption, and biologically implausible requirements (weight transport, non-locality, update locking, frozen activities).
motivation: Edge devices such as medical wearables and IoT sensors have memory budgets measured in megabytes and power budgets of 5-10W. Existing forward-only alternatives (FF, PEPITA, DRTP) only partially address BP's biological implausibility and achieve lower accuracy. A fully biologically-plausible, memory-efficient forward-only algorithm that approaches BP accuracy would enable viable on-device training.
method: Bio-FO trains each layer independently using only forward passes. For each hidden layer l, an auxiliary classifier with a fixed random matrix Bl projects layer activations hl to class predictions, computing local cross-entropy loss and gradient without backpropagating through other layers. Weight updates use only local activations (hl-1 and hl), avoiding weight transport (no symmetric backward weights), non-locality (no inter-layer error signals), update locking (updates proceed as activations arrive), and frozen activities (no activation storage required). A sparsity mask Sl enables locally connected (LC) and CNN extensions. Implemented in PyTorch; evaluated on MNIST, CIFAR-10/100, medical EEG/ECG datasets, and mini-ImageNet on NVIDIA Jetson Nano.
key_novelty: First forward-only algorithm to simultaneously and fully address all four biological implausibility issues of BP (weight transport, non-locality, update locking, frozen activities) while outperforming prior forward-only methods (FF, PEPITA, DRTP) in accuracy and achieving 3x memory reduction and up to 19.8x energy reduction.
contributions: Bio-FO: layer-local forward-only training with fixed random auxiliary classifiers
Simultaneous resolution of weight transport, non-locality, update locking, and frozen activities
3x memory reduction vs BP (32MB vs 96MB at batch size 1)
Up to 19.8x energy reduction vs FF on CIFAR-100 on Jetson Nano
Outperforms DRTP, PEPITA, FF on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, CHB-MIT, MIT-BIH, mini-ImageNet
Extension to LC and CNN via sparsity mask Sl
Fastest convergence among forward-only algorithms (lower slowness parameter)

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: Up to 19.8x energy reduction vs FF (CIFAR-100: 37.9 Wh vs 753.5 Wh for FF); evaluated at 5W power on Jetson Nano
metrics.accuracy: CIFAR-100: 74.57% error (vs 76.16% PEPITA, 85.76% FF); mini-ImageNet: 67.39% error (vs 74.58% CaFo, 91.23% PEPITA); 3x memory reduction vs BP
metrics.other: Fastest convergence: MNIST slowness 0.156 (vs 0.541 FF, 1.494 DRTP); hardware: NVIDIA Jetson Nano (128-core Maxwell GPU, 5-10W)

limitations: Accuracy gap vs BP remains significant on large-scale datasets (mini-ImageNet: 67.39% vs 53.49% error for BP)
Fixed random auxiliary classifiers may be suboptimal for complex tasks
Not yet evaluated on hardware designed specifically for forward-only algorithms
Not extended to GANs, GNNs, or Transformer architectures
Weight sharing in CNN extension is not biologically plausible
